findings.evidence: Live feature RPC: 64 enabled of 101 supported. Pinned features.macro parse: 64 DefaultYes. VHS /vote/test: all 64 at ledger 86785, 2026-02-09T14:31:12Z. The normal two-week majority activation path has never run on this network.
findings.remediation: Treat any future enablement that is not a single-amendment majority activation as an exceptional event; alert on any enabled-count change immediately.
findings.title: The enabled set is exactly the DefaultYes set, all enabled in one bulk event

findings.evidence: Live feature RPC returns only enabled/supported/name per amendment; no amendment carries a majority field. Vote counts (count/validations/threshold) are admin-only in AmendmentTable.cpp injectJson (lines 1000-1025). The earliest public signal of an approaching activation is the majority timestamp itself, which only appears once majority is already reached.
findings.remediation: Poll feature every flag interval (256 ledgers, ~12 min) and alert the moment any majority field appears; do not rely on vote-count trends, which the public RPC cannot show.
findings.title: Activation approach is invisible from the public RPC

findings.evidence: VHS /amendments/info lists 103 known amendments; the node's feature table lists 101 supported. Batch is registered in features.macro line 51 but Supported::no; OrchardPrivacy has 0 matches anywhere in the pinned source (fixtures/source-hashes.json absence_checks). The history service registry is newer than the node.
findings.remediation: Key monitoring to the node's own feature table, not the history service registry; flag any VHS-only name as drift, not as a pending activation.
findings.title: Registry drift: the history service knows amendments the node does not

findings.evidence: AmendmentTable.cpp needValidatedLedger only processes ledgers where (seq-1)/256 changes. From validated seq 8283007 the next flag ledger is 8283137, 130 ledgers (~371 s at the measured 2.857 s/ledger cadence).
findings.remediation: Schedule activation checks on flag ledgers, not wall-clock time; the response window after a majority-hold expiry is at most one flag interval (~12 min).
findings.title: Activation can only land at flag ledgers (256-ledger boundaries)

findings.evidence: Post-fix rule (fixAmendmentMajorityCalc enabled live): votes > floor(trusted*67/100). At 25 trusted validators 17 votes are needed — equal to validation quorum 17. At 24 trusted still 17; at 20 trusted 14; at 17 trusted 12 (drill A-01, 8/8 threshold checks).
findings.remediation: Alert when the trusted validator count drops below 25; recompute the activation bar on every UNL change.
findings.title: 17 of 25 trusted votes are needed, and the bar falls as the trusted set shrinks

findings.evidence: features.macro lines 45-46: PF_AccountExclusion and PF_ValidatorVoteTracking are Supported::yes, VoteBehavior::DefaultNo. Live feature RPC: both enabled=false. The gates they control (ValidatorVoteTracker.cpp:162; Change.cpp:618-619) never fire.
findings.remediation: Do not assume vote tracking or account exclusion is available; both need an explicit up-vote campaign plus a two-week majority hold to activate.
findings.title: Both PostFiat amendments are DefaultNo and disabled; the features they gate are inert

findings.evidence: AmendmentTable.cpp AmendmentState comment (lines 294-302): 'This is a one-way switch: once an amendment is enabled it can never be disabled, but it can be superseded by a subsequent amendment.' The only 'disable' match in the file is that comment (drill C-01).
findings.remediation: Before any up-vote, require a superseding amendment to exist or be drafted; treat activation as irreversible in the runbook.
findings.title: Enablement is one-way: a bad activation cannot be rolled back, only superseded

findings.evidence: features.macro has 16 XRPL_RETIRE entries; all 16 are disabled live. VHS marks 15 names deprecated and omits FlowCross, which the macro retires. Retired names still appear in registries and RPC output.
findings.remediation: Exclude retired names from activation watchlists; treat a retired name gaining a majority as a data error until proven otherwise.
findings.title: 16 retired amendments are all disabled, and the history service disagrees on one

findings.evidence: Live feature RPC disabled set includes MPTokensV1, NonFungibleTokensV1, PermissionedDEX, PermissionedDomains, SingleAssetVault, LendingProtocol, XChainBridge and TokenEscrow (all DefaultNo). No amendment has been enabled since the 2026-02-09 bulk event.
findings.remediation: Integrations must check enabled state per feature at runtime; never assume a named feature is live because the code ships it.
findings.title: 37 disabled amendments include major un-enabled features

findings.evidence: tx lookup for activation tx 0E373029EEF6AB43E24D5F1EAFBAEB80BBA9B94610BCE1A3D004101CCFAE7048 returns txnNotFound (error_code 29). The node's complete_ledgers range is 8200054-8283008, so ledger 86785 is outside retained history. VHS is the sole source for the activation ledger and date.
findings.remediation: Archive activation evidence outside the node (VHS export + this pack); do not expect the public node to serve old activation proofs.
findings.title: The 86785 activation transactions cannot be re-fetched from the public node

findings.evidence: SystemParameters.h:88 sets defaultAmendmentMajorityTime to 2 weeks. Config.cpp lines 870-898 parses amendment_majority_time (minutes/hours/days/weeks) and rejects values under 15 minutes. An operator config change can shrink the warning window from two weeks to 15 minutes.
findings.remediation: Monitor the node's configured majority time as part of the watch; a sub-two-week setting is itself an alert.
findings.title: The majority hold time is configurable down to 15 minutes

findings.evidence: outputs/postfiat_whitepaper.html (163,089 bytes) contains zero occurrences of 'amend'. No public document states which amendments the network intends to enable, in what order, or under what governance.
findings.remediation: Publish an amendment policy (intended set, vote order, veto criteria) before the first live majority activation.
findings.title: The whitepaper documents no amendment policy
